guideTitle: 6 Best Cheese Graters with Containers in 2026
metaDescription: Six handheld cheese graters with built in containers compared on capacity, lids, silicone bases and blade types, from Progressive to Lantana and Kunovo.
introParagraphs: A grater with its own container solves the most irritating part of grating: shreds scattering across the board and a second dish to wash. The six picks here take different approaches. The Progressive PrepSolutions 2-Way stores a 2 cup container inside the grater, the Lantana adds a hexagonal measuring container and six grating functions, the Svailse uses a stainless steel bowl, and the Kunovo, KEISSCO and KitchenBe1 use BPA free plastic containers with lids.

We compared them on container material and capacity, lid fit for fridge storage, the grating blades themselves and how securely each sits while you work. Most of these are flat plate or bowl style graters rather than four sided boxes, so they take less drawer space than a box grater but offer fewer faces.

If you grate cheese ahead of meals, or want to store leftover shreds, a container model is the sensible category. The tables near the end help you choose by capacity, lid style and the extra tools that come in the box.

products.name: Progressive PrepSolutions 2-Way Grate and Measure
products.description:
The PrepSolutions 2-Way is a grate and measure tool: you grate directly into a removable measuring container that holds up to 2 cups, and the container stores neatly inside the grater when you are done. The listing mentions fine and medium grating surfaces, a no mess approach and an ergonomic design for shredding cheese, vegetables and chocolate.

The nesting design is the biggest practical advantage, and it is the reason this tool earns the top spot over fancier options. A grater with a separate container usually means two pieces to find, but here everything lives as one unit in a drawer. The limits are the two blade options, which do not include a coarse shred or slicer, and the 2 cup limit, which is fine for a recipe but small for a party. Plastic parts also need gentle cleaning.

Compared with the Lantana, it has fewer functions and a simpler look. Compared with the Svailse, it uses a plastic container and a more compact build. For everyday cooks who want a straightforward grate and measure tool, it is the neatest choice. A good habit is to grate over the container on a flat counter, tap the plate against the rim, then snap the container out and use the markings to check the amount before it goes into the pan.
products.bestFor: Everyday cooks who want grating and measuring in one unit.
pros: Fine and medium surfaces cover common jobs
Ergonomic shape suits cheese, vegetables and chocolate
cons: No coarse shred or slicing surface
Two cup capacity is small for large batches

products.name: Lantana 6 in 1 Cheese Grater with Container
products.description:
The Lantana offers six functions in a handheld grater: coarse, medium and fine grating among them, according to the listing. It comes with a fitted hexagonal container that measures and holds the shreds, and a non slip, non scratch silicone rubber base for a secure grip on counters and a snug fit to the container.

The silicone base is the feature that sets it apart. It stops the grater from sliding as you work and protects countertops, which matters because container graters can be top heavy once they fill. Six functions are generous for a handheld tool, but they come with more surfaces to clean, and the hexagonal container is not as compact as a nesting design.

Compared with the PrepSolutions, it offers more cuts and a stronger grip. Compared with the Kunovo, it has a more structured, premium feel. It sits at the top of the price scale in our data, so it suits people who want one handheld tool with lots of options. Because the container is fitted rather than nested, give it a permanent spot in a drawer and wash the silicone base separately so cheese oil does not collect in the join.
products.bestFor: Cooks wanting many cuts and a stable, non slip base.
pros: Six grating functions in one tool
Fitted container measures and holds shreds
cons: Priced above most container graters here
More surfaces to clean than simpler models

products.name: Svailse Box Cheese Grater with Container
products.description:
The Svailse is described as a four in one set: three grating types, fine, medium and coarse, plus a lid, with grated food falling directly into a stainless steel container. The listing says it suits hard and soft cheese, ginger, garlic, nutmeg, chocolate and citrus fruit, and calls out a light green finish for a colourful kitchen.

A stainless container is a different proposition from plastic, since it will not stain or hold smells and can be washed hot. It is also heavier, and the metal to metal contact can be noisy as you work. The lid helps with fridge storage, but the listing does not give a capacity figure, so check dimensions on the page if portion size matters.

Compared with the PrepSolutions, it adds a coarse surface and a metal bowl. If you grate a lot of hard cheese for baked pasta, the extra coarse side makes the difference. Compared with the KEISSCO, it avoids plastic entirely. It suits cooks who dislike plastic and want a durable catch bowl. Wipe the bowl dry before closing the lid, since a damp stainless interior can trap moisture against the cheese and shorten its fridge life.
products.bestFor: Cooks who avoid plastic and want a metal catch bowl.
pros: Stainless steel container resists stains and odours
Fine, medium and coarse grating surfaces
Grates cheese, ginger, nutmeg and zest
cons: Capacity is not given in the listing
Metal bowl is heavier than plastic

products.name: Kunovo Stainless Steel Cheese Grater with Airtight Container
products.description:
The Kunovo pairs a stainless steel grating plate with a BPA free polypropylene storage container that the listing calls airtight. It offers two sizes of stainless steel grating flakes, and the maker says you can use it for potatoes, carrots and other vegetables as well as cheese like Parmesan and cheddar.

The airtight seal is the selling point: you can grate straight into the container, snap the lid on and refrigerate. Two blade sizes are fewer than the Lantana or Svailse, so slicing and extra coarse cuts are out. The plastic container can pick up cheese odours over time, and the listing does not give a capacity figure.

Compared with the KEISSCO, it is more basic and focuses on storage. Compared with the Svailse, it uses plastic rather than a metal bowl. It suits people who grate ahead and store, such as meal preppers. Fill it only to the shoulder of the container so the lid closes without pressing on the shreds, and press out a little air before sealing.
products.bestFor: Meal preppers who grate ahead and store in the fridge.
pros: Two blade sizes for common grating
cons: No slicing or extra coarse surface
Capacity not stated in the listing

products.name: KEISSCO Cheese Grater and Lemon Zester with Container
products.description:
The KEISSCO is a flat grater and zester that attaches to a container base for mess free grating, and a lid closes the container for storage. The listing describes razor sharp stainless steel blades with fine and coarse grates, and says it handles hard Parmesan or soft cheddar as well as citrus.

Because it combines grating and zesting, it is a flexible tool for small jobs such as lemon zest on a salad and parmesan over pasta. The flat plate style is easy to rinse, but the container must be taken apart to clean the underside. It is a simple design without the nesting or measuring marks of the PrepSolutions.

Compared with the Kunovo, it has the zester feel and a wider plate. The plate sits flat on the container, which makes it simple to line up over a pot or salad bowl when you want the zest to land directly on the food. Compared with the Lantana, it has fewer cuts. It is a good choice for people who want a compact container grater that also zests. Zest lemons and limes first, then switch to cheese, because citrus oils can flavour the next thing you grate.
products.bestFor: Small jobs like Parmesan, citrus zest and quick toppings.
cons: Simple plate has fewer cut types

products.name: KitchenBe1 Cheese Grater with Container and Peeler Set
products.description:
The KitchenBe1 is a set rather than a single tool: a multi function food grater with a BPA free polypropylene container and a fitted white lid, plus a peeler. The idea, as the listing describes it, is to peel a vegetable, grate it and close the container straight away, whether you are working with potatoes, onions or cheese.

Having a peeler in the box turns it into a small prep kit, which is helpful for people setting up a kitchen or giving a gift. The grater itself is a basic handheld plate, so it will not match the cut range of the Lantana. The lid fits snugly, but capacity details are not in the text we have. Treat the container as a prep and short term storage bowl rather than a place to keep cheese for a week.

Compared with the Kunovo, it adds a peeler. Compared with the PrepSolutions, it is less refined but more of a bundle. It sits fairly high in the price range in our data, which makes sense as a set. The peeler is a handy bonus for potatoes and carrots, though it is a separate tool and does not change the way the grater performs.
products.bestFor: Setting up a kitchen or giving a prep tool bundle.
pros: Works on cheese, potatoes and onions
cons: Capacity not given in the listing

buyingCriteria.explanation: Capacity decides how often you stop to empty the container. The PrepSolutions holds 2 cups, which suits most recipes, while other listings do not state a figure. If you shred for a family, a bigger container is useful. For toppings, a smaller one is fine and stores more easily. Check the dimensions on the product page before buying. A container that looks large in a photo may hold less than a cup of loosely packed shreds, because fluffy fine gratings take more room than coarse ones. Match the capacity to the biggest recipe you cook, not the average one.

Plastic containers such as the Kunovo, KEISSCO and KitchenBe1 are light and cheap, while the Svailse uses stainless steel. Plastic can hold odours and stain with strongly coloured foods over time. Stainless resists both but is heavier. Choose based on whether you plan to store cheese in it. If the container is only a catch tray that you empty at once, either material is fine, and the lighter plastic is easier to hold in one hand.

A lid turns a grating tool into a storage tool. The Kunovo calls its container airtight and the KitchenBe1 includes a fitted lid. Grated cheese keeps best in the refrigerator and is best used within a few days. Avoid leaving it on the counter. If you freeze surplus shreds, spread them on a tray first so they do not clump into one block, then bag them.

The Lantana offers six functions, the Svailse three grating types, and the PrepSolutions two. Fine and coarse are the most used. If you want slicing, check that the listing includes a slicing surface. Many handheld container models are strictly graters, so a mandoline or a box grater is still the better tool for even slices. Count your regular tasks first and buy the surfaces that match them.

A grater that slides is annoying and risky. The Lantana has a silicone base, and the PrepSolutions has an ergonomic shape. A non slip base matters most when the container fills and gets top heavy. Grate on a stable board. If your tool tends to creep, place a damp cloth beneath it, and keep the cutting hand curled so that the last bit of cheese is never pushed with bare fingertips.

Container graters have more parts. Rinse the plate and container right after use, and use a brush on the holes. Check dishwasher guidance for each listing, since plastic can warp in high heat. Nested designs like the PrepSolutions are quicker to wash as a single unit.

faq.q: Why use a grater with a container?
faq.a: A container catches the shreds, keeps the counter clean and lets you measure or store the cheese. It cuts down on washing a second bowl, and it also reduces the cheese that ends up on the floor or the board. It also helps with recipes that specify an amount of cheese, because you can read the level on the side of the container and stop at exactly the amount you need rather than guessing.

faq.q: How long can I keep grated cheese?
faq.a: Grated cheese keeps best sealed in the refrigerator and is best used within a few days. Grating just before cooking gives the best texture and flavour. Avoid leaving it on a warm counter.

Containers listed as BPA free polypropylene are a common choice for food storage. Avoid high heat in the dishwasher unless the listing says it is safe. Hand washing the container in warm water is gentler and usually only takes a minute. If you prefer to avoid plastic, the Svailse stainless bowl is an alternative.

faq.q: Can I grate soft cheese with these?
faq.a: Soft cheese works better when chilled for about fifteen minutes in the freezer, and a coarse surface clogs less. Very soft cheese is easier to slice or crumble. Hard cheese is the easiest to grate. Semi hard cheeses such as young cheddar sit in the middle and do well on the coarse side with a cold block.

faq.q: How do I clean the holes?
faq.a: Rinse immediately and use a small brush from the back of the plate. Dried cheese is hard to remove, so do not leave it to sit. A used toothbrush works well for the fine holes, and a quick soak loosens anything that has already hardened. Dry before storage. For plastic containers, a baking soda rinse now and then helps remove cheese smells that linger after many uses.

faq.q: Do container graters suit weak hands?
faq.a: They are lighter than box graters but still need a steady push, and the container adds a little weight as it fills. Empty it often rather than grating a full two cups in one go. A non slip base like the Lantana helps. If you have a medical concern, ask a doctor or occupational therapist which grater suits you.
